basis: Dural vascular malformation; hydrocephalus and CNS cysts occur in 30-79%, supporting neurologic involvement. Tinnitus alone does not establish ear damage.
Developmental impairment, hypotonia and seizures define the syndrome; additional congenital organ anomalies vary across subtypes.
Autoimmune lupus with prominent skin and joint disease; cytopenias affect roughly half of systemic cases. Renal involvement varies across subtypes and is omitted at the cap.
Congenital heart disease, radioulnar synostosis and intellectual disability define the syndrome.
Autoimmune platelet destruction; purpura is a bleeding sign. Arterial thrombosis is a separately diagnosed complication rather than defining organ involvement.
Familial lateral femoral cutaneous nerve neuropathy.
Congenital antecubital skin webbing with restricted elbow extension and radioulnar joint maldevelopment defines the syndrome.
Polyosteolysis and hyperostosis are defining structural bone abnormalities.
Elevated pulmonary vascular pressure is cardiovascular disease; underlying lung disease is separately diagnosed and varies by subtype.
Congenital structural abnormality of the superior vena cava or its venous connections.
Invasive carcinoma originating in urinary tract urothelium, including bladder, renal pelvis and ureter.
Persistent postpartum amenorrhea and galactorrhea associated with acquired hyperprolactinemia establish an endocrine disorder.
Inherited abnormalities of skeletal growth and development define this umbrella; extraskeletal involvement varies by subtype.
Intellectual disability and seizures define the neurologic phenotype; characteristic hypogammaglobulinemia supports immunodeficiency. Skeletal involvement has uncertain frequency.
Inherited renal tubular amino-acid reabsorption defect; usually asymptomatic, without established common neurologic or ocular damage.
Lung agenesis, congenital cardiac defects and thumb malformations constitute the defining syndrome.
Inherited peripheral neuropathy with distal muscle wasting and weakness in 20/20 patients. Cataracts and neutropenia lack evidence of occurrence in at least 30%.
Carcinoma originating in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the defined axes.
Inherited neurodevelopmental syndrome; no additional organ involvement is established across the umbrella.
Defining cerebral malformation with severe intellectual disability, spasticity and seizures; cardiac, ocular and skeletal findings are optional associations.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability in 9/9 patients; behavioral findings add no organ axis, and the gene alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Xanthogranulomatous inflammation of a salivary gland; neither infection nor an autoimmune mechanism is established.
Hepatic fatty-acid oxidation defect; neurologic deficits including hemiparesis occur in 30-79%, muscle atrophy in 80-99%. Renal tubular acidosis occurs in 5-29%.
Metaphyseal bone dysplasia, anetoderma with dermal elastic-tissue loss, and optic atrophy define the syndrome.
Rickettsial infection directly injures vascular endothelium, causing systemic small-vessel vasculitis. Rash is transient; severe additional organ injury affects a minority.
